intent: Remove the four unused Flutter platform runner directories from billsplit so the repo tracks only the android target it actually ships, and so the last over-cap C++ file disappears without hand-editing generated scaffolding.
scope: Deleted billsplit/windows/ (18 files), billsplit/macos/ (28), billsplit/ios/ (40), billsplit/linux/ (10) - 96 tracked files, 4188 lines
Unpicked the three places that referenced them: .gitignore un-ignore rules, .binary-allowlist icon entries, billsplit/README.md
Non-goal: billsplit/android/ stays tracked; no lib/ or test/ change; no CI workflow change
changes: git rm -r on the four platform dirs. Nothing built them: .github/workflows/billsplit-ci.yml runs pub get, dart format, flutter analyze, flutter test and the Python coverage gate, with no flutter build step for any platform. A repo-wide grep found no script or doc invoking a build for them either.

Removed the four .binary-allowlist entries (ios/macos AppIcon+LaunchImage PNGs, windows app_icon.ico) and the four .gitignore un-ignore rules that existed solely to let those icons past the repo's binary block.
Added billsplit/ios/, billsplit/macos/, billsplit/windows/, billsplit/linux/ as .gitignore entries so a stray `flutter create` regenerates them locally without them becoming tracked files again.

Rewrote the billsplit/README.md Running section: it claimed the repo ships without platform runner folders, which was false while 96 of them were tracked and is now true again except for android. Documents that the regenerated dirs are gitignored and that CI never builds them.

Left billsplit/analysis_options.yaml alone. An edit removing the now-dead ios/macos/windows/linux/web excludes was attempted and `flutter analyze` immediately rewrote the file back (it prints 'Upgrading analysis_options.yaml to exclude build and platform directories'). The excludes are regenerated by Flutter tooling, so removing them is not durable and fighting it would produce a permanently dirty file.

verification.evidence: 41 over-cap files before, 40 after. grep -c win32_window on the same output returns 0, so billsplit/windows/runner/win32_window.cpp (288 lines, over by 38) is gone from the list. The C++ category is now empty; the remaining 40 are 29 shell, 7 python, 2 kotlin, 1 dart, 1 markdown.
exit 0, 'No issues found!' - unchanged from the green baseline established in the preceding commit. Deleting the dirs introduced no analyzer regression.
60 tests passed, the same count as before the deletion. An unchanged count is the discriminating check that no test file lived under the removed directories.

verification.command: cd billsplit && flutter create . --platforms=linux,windows,macos,ios ; git add -An billsplit/{windows,macos,ios,linux}
verification.evidence: This is the check that the resurrection guard actually works, and it is the only one git can perform. After really regenerating all four directories on disk, `git add -An` refuses every one: 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: billsplit/ios, billsplit/linux, billsplit/macos, billsplit/windows'. git status --untracked-files=all over those paths shows nothing beyond the staged deletions. git check-ignore -v names the new rules at .gitignore:406-409. The regenerated dirs were then deleted again, and the .metadata and pubspec.lock files that flutter create had modified as a side effect were reverted with git checkout.

risks: Anyone wanting to run billsplit on linux/macos/windows/iOS must now run `flutter create . --platforms=...` first. The README documents this. The regenerated scaffolding is Flutter-standard, so nothing hand-written is lost - that is precisely why these files were safe to delete rather than split.

billsplit/linux/ was deleted on the evidence that nothing references it, not on positive proof it is unused. If the Linux desktop build turns out to be wanted, `flutter create . --platforms=linux` restores it in seconds and it will simply stay untracked.

The macos and ios AppIcon assets are gone from the repo. They are regenerable from billsplit/assets/icon/ via the shared generator in python_pkg/app_icons/, which is still tracked and still covers billsplit.
rollback: git revert the commit. All 96 files return, along with the .gitignore un-ignore rules, the .binary-allowlist entries and the old README text.

After rollback, confirm check_file_length.sh --all reports 41 over-cap files with win32_window.cpp among them, and that flutter analyze and flutter test are still clean - the revert should not disturb either, since no code under lib/ or test/ is involved.
